column4: Dialect-arm SUBTESTS of the cleat#3409 tests: each arm opens its own database and skips when its DSN is not set, so in a PostgreSQL-only job the MySQL and SQL Server arms skip while the PostgreSQL tests RUN. The parent tests report PASS, so the skip names carry the arm suffix (cleat#3437). Measured by name: CLEAT_TEST_POSTGRES=<pg> go test ./engine/ -run 'TestCompactHistory(Compacts|RollsBack|AndFinalize)' -json | grep '"Action":"skip"' -- 8 skips on this machine, 3+2+3 across the three tests; PostgreSQL, MySQL 8.4 and SQL Server 2022 all local. The count here is per test (3, 2, 3), declared as three lines.

The three PostgreSQL-only cleat#3409 tests (newRunTestStore -> testutil.TestDB(t, DialectPostgres), no subtest split). This job sets only one other DSN, so they skip as whole tests. Measured by name with only the other DSN set: 3 whole-test skips.

The SQL Server arms of the cleat#3409 dialect tests, in the MySQL-only job: mssql_rcsi_on and mssql_rcsi_off each open a private database, so they skip without CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL. mssql_rcsi_on runs the lost-fence test too; mssql_rcsi_off does not (its plain generation read waits for the reclaim, so there is no window; see the test). Measured by name with only CLEAT_TEST_MYSQL set: 2 + 1 + 2 = 5 skips.
